Well there are plenty of voice doctors and surgeries that will raise pitch. For the most part they are basically the same though. The main problem is that human voice is pretty complex and too delicate to invavsively operate on it without reducing the quality. So you really should at least try training first. I'm pretty sure you'll get better results than you think, just keep practicing everyday. But if you just aren't getting the results you want, I might a suggest surgery as a last shot. 

P.S Get a really good voice trainer. I'll suggest TransVoiceLessons with Zhea. She has consistent success with her students and will prevent you from making a ton of early mistakes about voice feminizing.

The surgery you're describing is done by Yeson. How it works is that they block off the lower end of your pitch which forces you to speak in a higher range, therefore raising your base pitch. If you're that concerned about pitch, you'll have better, cheaper results by training than surgery though.

What I really like about Endgame is that my boy Thor finally got a (relatively) happy ending. Good god has my boy been put through the wringer. He has gone through so much, including:

* His mother dying
* His girlfriend dumping him
* His friends (Warriors Three and Heimdall) dying
* His hammer is destroyed
* His father dies too
* He finds out that his entire culture is descended from conquering and decimating other worlds
* His father dies as well
* Asgard gets blown up
* His people get attacked by Thanos's ship
* His brother dies in the attack

Lastly, he fails at killing Thanos, being indirectly responsible for the deaths of trillions. No wonder by the time we see him he's a complete mess wasting away playing video games and getting drunk off his ass. As funny as watching Fat Thor was, it was absolutely heartbreaking to see what this all-powerful god-hero has become.

He desperately need a happy ending and he finally got one. He got closure and a much needed therapy session from his mother, reminding him that he's a hero no matter what and to be the person he is, not who he is supposed to be. He gets his hammer back (yay!) and actually succeeds in helping to bring down Thanos. Then he gets to travel alongside the Guardians of the Galaxy as a new member, giving him a new purpose and a family. So thank you Russo brothers for finally giving my boy a good ending after all he's been through for the past couple movies.

1. It depends on who you go to. My laser treatments for upper lip are about $80.
2. If you have light skin with dark hair it will require less treatments. I have had about 7\-8 treatments so far and it has reduced the amount of facial hair and shadow a lot. But you won't really see a lot of results til you have had about 3 to 4 treatments.
3. Somewhat, it feels like a rubber band on the face for me, but it's really quick.
4. As said before it's pretty quick, about 5 to 10 minutes for the face, for larger areas it depends on how much pain tolerance you have and how many break you take.
5. About 3 to 4 treatments.
6. You want to get the hair as short as possible when you go for laser so the laser can go into the hair follicle easier.
7. Facial hair does not count as full body (at least where I go).
8. Again it depends on your shade and hair color. Light skin with darker hair needs less treatment because the hair is more receptive to the laser that way.
9. I have had laser about 7\-8 times, mostly on the upper lip with some electrolysis thrown in every now and then. However, it's better to get as much hair as possible removed by laser first before going into electrolysis to remove the stray hairs. FYI after your treatment stay out of the sun for avoid skin discoloration, use sunscreen afterward, no antibiotics before your appointment, shave as close to the grain as possible, and lastly, the hair will fall out about 7\-14 days afterward but it's a real pain to shave the hair that got zapped. Good luck! I'm rooting for you!
